transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning roundtable for the proposed six-week peer-tutoring program for grades 6 through 8. As you know, before I can sign off on the final plan, I need to gather relevant information from each of you in your respective areas. I'd like to go around the table and hear your input on the draft plan — specifically regarding the two adult supervisors, the use of Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and the paper consent forms. Let's start with the teacher — what are your thoughts and any recommendations from an instructional standpoint?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an important staffing issue. I received the finalized roster from the activities office yesterday, and it contains 18 student tutors. However, the school's supervision rule permits one adult to supervise no more than six tutors in an active tutoring session. That means with 18 tutors, we'd need at least three adult supervisors — not two as the draft plan currently states. The draft plan still lists the preliminary staffing estimate of two supervisors, so this needs to be updated before the program can be approved.

transcript.text: I need to raise a concern about the student-selected tutor pairings. My student-support review, which I completed this week, found two active no-contact restrictions involving prospective tutors and students seeking tutoring. These restrictions are currently recorded only in confidential counseling files, so others wouldn't be aware of them. Because of these restrictions, tutor pairings cannot be left to student selection — they must be assigned and monitored by me as counselor to ensure we don't violate those no-contact orders.

Ms. Brooks, you've flagged two active no-contact restrictions that mean tutor pairings must be counselor-assigned rather than student-selected. Mr. Ortiz, you've noted that Google Classroom is not approved and we need to use the district-managed Microsoft Teams education environment instead. And Ms. Walker, you've indicated that consent must be entered in the student information system, and that electronic translated forms are available in addition to paper forms. Before I finalize the approval, I want to make sure each of these recommendations is clearly attributed to its source for the approval minutes.
